lines: אישׁ 45 אית
man of God, i. q. servant and minister
of God ; spoken of angels Judg. 13, 6. 8 ;
of prophets 1 Sam. 2, 27 ; of Moses
Deut. 33, 1 ; of David 2 Chr. 8, 14.   k)
With genit. of an attribute, quality, vir-
tue, vice, etc. it denotes one possess-
ing that attribute or quality ; and in
this way the Hebrews form a peri-
phrasis for an adjective ; e. g. אִישׁ תֹּאַר
a man of form, i. e. handsome ; אִישׁ דָּמִים
a man of blood, bloody ; אַנְשֵׁי לֵבָב intel-
ligent, see in לֵב no. 1. e ; אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם men
of name, famous, Gen. 6, 4 ; comp. אִישׁ
הָאֲדָמָה a husbandman, Gen. 9, 20.   l)
Collect. for men, i. e. soldiers, troops, Is.
21, 9. Comp. אָדָם Is. 22, 6. m) אִישׁ
marks also a man of rank, a great man,
noble, as opp. to אָדָם a man of low con-
dition ; see in אָדָם no. 1. b. n) As joined
with numerals, we find after numerals
below ten אֲנָשִׁים, as שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲנָשִׁים Gen.
18, 2 ; between ten and twenty some-
times אִישׁ, Num. 1, 44 ; and above twen-
ty always אִישׁ, 1 Sam. 14, 14. 22, 2. 18.
al. sæp.
2. With אָח or רֵעַ, one—another ; see
אָח and רֵעַ.
3. Put for any man, i. e. one, some one,
any one, Gen. 13, 16. Ex. 16, 29. Cant.
8, 7. So Syr. ܐ݇ܢܳܫ for τὶς, e. g. ܝܗܘܕܝܐ
ܐ݇ܢܳܫ a certain Jew. Plur. אֲנָשִׁים men,
certain men, like Syr. ܐ݇ܢܳܫܺܝ̈ܢ, 1 K. 20,
4. each, every one. 1 K. 20, 20 וַיַּכּוּ
אִישׁ אִישׁוֹ and they slew every one his
man. אִישׁ וְאִישׁ this and that man, each
and every one, Ps. 87, 5. Esth. 1, 8.
Once like כֹּל prefixed to another subst.
Gen. 15, 10 וַיִּתֵּן אִישׁ־בִּתְרוֹ לִקְרַאת רֵעֵהוּ
and laid each part of each (animal) one
over against the other, where אִישׁ־בִּתְרוֹ
is i. q. כָּל־בִּתְרוֹ, but the sacred writer
puts אִישׁ for כֹּל in order to correspond
with the following רֵעֵהוּ. So too אִישׁ
אָחִיו Gen. 9, 5.
5. Impers. like Germ. man, Fr. on,
Engl. one, plur. men, e. g. one says, men
say, etc. 1 Sam. 9, 9 לְפָנִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כֹּה
אָמַר אִישׁ formerly in Israel men said
thus, i. q. it was said.
6. בְּנֵי אִישׁ sons of men, as a peri-
phrastic plur. for men simply, Ps. 4, 3;
like בְּנֵי אָדָם, see אָדָם no. 5.—Sometimes
emphat. for the noble, the high, opp. to
בְּנֵי אָדָם, Ps. 49, 3. Prov. 8, 4 ; see no. 1.
m, and אָדָם no. 1. b.
Note. As to the etymology, we hold
אִישׁ to be a primitive word ; yet soft-
ened from the harsher form אֱנָשׁ (אָנַשׁ)
q. v. whence also אִשָּׁה for אִנְשָׁה, and
plur. אֲנָשִׁים . In like manner the Arabic
has إِنْسَانٌ and إِيسَانٌ .
Deriv. אִישׁוֹן, pr. n. אִישְׁהוֹד, אִישׁ־בּשֶׁת,
also
אִישׁ denom. verb, only in Hithpal.
הִתְאוֹשֵׁשׁ to show oneself a man, ἀνδρί-
ζεσθαι; Is. 46, 8 הִתְאֹשָׁשׁוּ show your-
selves men, be men, i. e. be wise, cast
away the childish trifles of idolaters.
Chald. הִתְאַשֵּׁשׁ and הִתְאֹשֵׁשׁ id.
אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת (man of shame, i. e. sham-
ing himself, perh. bashful,) pr. n. Ishbo-
sheth, the son of Saul, who for two years
after the death of his father and brothers
reigned over eleven tribes in opposition
to David. 2 Sam. c. 2–4.
אִישְׁהוֹד (man of glory) Ishhod, pr. n.
אִישׁוֹן m. (dimin. from אִישׁ) 1. a
little man, manikin, homunculus, and
with עַיִן the little man of the eye, i. e. the
pupil, apple of the eye, in which, as in
a mirror, a person sees his own image
reflected in miniature. Deut. 32, 10.
Prov. 7, 2. This pleasing image is
found in several languages; e. g. Arab.
إِنْسَانُ ٱلْعَيْنِ homunculus oculi, Gr.
κόρη, κοράσιον, κορασίδιον, Lat. pupa,
pupula, pupilla, Pers. مردك ; see more
in Thesaur. p. 86.—More fully Ps. 17, 8
אִישׁוֹן בַּת עַיִן i. e. the pupil, daughter of
the eye ; see in בַּת no. 7.
2. Metaph. the middle, the midst of
any thing, like Arab. نُونُو apple of the
eye, for the midst, the summit.—Hence
Prov. 7, 9 in the eye-ball (pupil) of the
night, i. e. at midnight. 20, 20 in the very
eye-ball of darkness, i. e. in the midst of
darkness ; where in Keri is read בֶּאֱשׁוּן ח׳
in the darkness of night.
אִישַׁי Chald. for יִשַׁי Jesse, 1 Chr. 2,
אִיתוֹן for אָתִיוֹן m. Ez. 40, 15 Keri,
an entrance, from r. אָתָה i. q. בּוֹא to
